name: Make internal public equity investment decisions
summary: Internal portfolio managers run factor, index, portfolio completion and fundamental strategies inside the public equity pools and decide which stocks to buy or sell. Most orders come in lists from a monthly factor rebalance or an index change, where an analyst checks data, the portfolio manager runs the model and reviews the trade list and a managing director signs off; fewer orders come from fundamental research, which takes far longer per order and may need managing director or committee approval and a compliance check for inside information. Every order is staged in the order management system, passes pre-trade compliance and is released to the trading desk; data problems, false compliance alerts and waits for index effective dates and approvals drive the elapsed time.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian provincial public-sector asset manager with about 240 staff whose public equities team runs internal factor, index, completion and fundamental strategies inside three equity pools next to external managers.
baseline.notes: Snapshot end 2021; public equities $26.3 billion, of which the equity pools held about $25.2 billion.

trigger: A scheduled factor rebalance, an index or corporate action change, a fundamental research conclusion, or a compliance exception requiring a corrective trade.
end_state: The order has been released to the trading desk and the resulting position checked against target the next day; or the decision is declined, blocked or the order cancelled.

volume.seasonality: Peaks at month end (factor rebalances), at index review effective dates in February, May, August and November, and when pools receive large flows.

evidence.note: Organisation file: about two thirds of 900 internal public market orders a month are equity; program lists counted as one order per security.

steps.name: An order need arises
steps.description: A need for an equity order appears: the monthly factor rebalance date arrives, an index provider announces constituent changes or a corporate action changes index weights, the fundamental team concludes research on a company, or compliance reports a guideline breach that needs a corrective trade. The order management system and team calendar route the work to the right strategy team.

next.condition: corrective trade for a guideline breach

evidence.note: Strategy mix (fundamental, factor, index, completion) is from the model manager; the shares of orders by strategy are the author's estimate. Factor and index lists produce many single-security orders.

steps.name: Refresh and check model input data
steps.description: Before the scheduled rebalance the analyst loads prices, fundamentals, factor scores, index weights and security reference data from the data warehouse and vendor feeds into the model, and checks for missing, stale or extreme values, new listings and pending corporate actions, sending data problems to investment data management. Touch time is this order's share of work done for a whole rebalance list, so it is small per order.

error.defect_description: A stale price or wrong share count passes into the model.

evidence.note: Factor strategies target size, quality, value and momentum attributes; data checks are the author's description of common quantitative practice.

steps.name: Run the factor model and optimiser
steps.description: The portfolio manager runs the scoring model and the portfolio optimiser with the strategy's risk model and constraints (tracking error, factor exposures, sector and name limits, turnover and liquidity), and reviews the target portfolio and the resulting trade list. Touch time is this order's share of work done for a whole rebalance list, so it is small per order.

error.defect_description: A constraint set wrongly, giving too much turnover or an unintended exposure.

evidence.note: Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the proposed trade list
steps.description: The portfolio manager screens the list name by name: drops trades too small to be worth the cost, holds names with pending takeovers or index events, checks sizes against average daily volume and decides whether illiquid names should be spread over several days. Touch time is this order's share of work done for a whole rebalance list, so it is small per order.

evidence.note: Order size relative to daily volume and urgency drive the trading horizon.

steps.name: Managing director signs off the rebalance summary
steps.description: The managing director reviews a one-page summary of the rebalance (turnover, expected cost, tracking error, factor and sector shifts) and approves it by email or asks for a rerun. Touch time is this order's share of work done for a whole rebalance list, so it is small per order.

control.basis: Strategy procedures: rebalance summary approved by the head of the strategy before orders are created (author's assumption)

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the model manager does not publish its rebalance approval steps.

steps.name: Work out trades from index and corporate action changes
steps.description: The analyst reads the index provider's announcement or the corporate action notice, builds the pro forma index weights, and calculates the buys and sells the index or completion sleeve needs, including trades to invest dividends or small flows, in a spreadsheet linked to holdings.

error.defect_description: Wrong pro forma weight or share count for an index change.

evidence.note: MSCI reviews indexes each February, May, August and November with set announcement and effective dates.

steps.name: Decide timing for index sleeve trades
steps.description: Near the effective date the portfolio manager decides whether to trade at the effective-date close to keep tracking error low, to pre-position some names, or to leave small differences, and sets the order instructions.

evidence.note: Index funds typically use the closing price benchmark; wait is until the effective date (index changes are announced about two to three weeks ahead; flow trades the same day).

steps.name: Research the company and update the valuation model
steps.description: The fundamental analyst updates the company model (discounted cash flow, comparables), reads filings and industry data, joins meetings with management and sell-side analysts, notes environmental, social and governance issues and writes up the investment case for an addition, a trim or a new position.

error.defect_description: Model error or stale estimate that misstates value.

evidence.note: Time per order is the author's estimate; research also runs between orders.

steps.name: Decide the position change and its size
steps.description: The portfolio manager challenges the research, decides the target position size within the strategy's limits and the entry or exit plan (limit price, horizon, urgency), and records the rationale in the research file.

next.condition: new position or above the portfolio manager's limit

evidence.note: Fundamental team makes a small number of sizable investments; shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Managing director approves a new or large position
steps.description: The managing director reviews the research note and sizing for a new holding or a change above the portfolio manager's limit and approves, asks for more work, or sends very large stakes to the department committee.

control.basis: Approval authorities in the model manager's investment approval framework (department level; thresholds not published)

evidence.note: The model manager states approval authorities between the Board, the Management Investment Committee and Investment Department Committees are defined; the split is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Equities and Credit committee approves a large stake
steps.description: For a large ownership stake, for example one that may bring board representation, the Equities and Credit Investment Department Committee, co-chaired by investments and investment risk with legal and responsible investing present, hears the team at its next meeting and approves, attaches conditions or declines.

control.basis: The model manager Investment Approval Policy: Investment Department Committees approve decisions up to set thresholds; larger ones go to the Management Investment Committee and the Board

next.condition: conditions require a smaller or phased position

steps.name: Check restricted list, inside information and ownership limits
steps.description: A compliance analyst checks the company against the restricted and watch lists (for example after a management meeting that may have passed inside information, or where the model manager has a board nominee), the pool's ownership threshold limits and any client exclusion, and clears or holds the trade.

control.basis: Securities law prohibition on trading with undisclosed material information and the OSC exemption order's conflict policies (insider trading, front running)

evidence.note: Hold rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Decide the corrective trade for a guideline breach
steps.description: When compliance reports a breach (for example a holding pushed over an issuer limit by a market move or a corporate action), the portfolio manager agrees with compliance how and by when to cure it and sizes the corrective sale or purchase.

control.basis: OSC exemption order condition: policies preventing investments that contravene the restrictions in each investment management agreement; breaches cured and reported

steps.name: Create and stage the orders in the OMS
steps.description: The portfolio manager uploads the optimiser or index trade file into the order management system, or keys a fundamental order by hand, choosing the pool or client account, side, quantity and the instructions for the desk (urgency, benchmark such as arrival price or close, limit price).

error.defect_description: Wrong quantity, side or account (fat finger) or a missing limit.

evidence.note: Instructions carry the portfolio manager's urgency and benchmark to the trader.

steps.name: Pre-trade compliance check
steps.description: The order management system tests each staged order against coded restrictions for the pool or account (restricted list, issuer and ownership limits, prohibited instruments, cash) and passes it, warns or blocks.

control.basis: OSC exemption order condition on preventing contraventions of investment restrictions; SOC 1 objective that trades follow portfolio guidelines

evidence.note: Alert rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Compliance clears or rejects the alert
steps.description: A compliance analyst checks whether the warning is a real breach or a reference data problem (unclassified new security, stale share count) and records an override with the reason, or rejects the order back to the portfolio manager.

control.basis: Soft-block overrides decided and logged by compliance, not by the portfolio manager

steps.name: Portfolio manager checks and releases the orders
steps.description: The portfolio manager looks over the staged orders (sides, sizes against daily volume, accounts, instructions) and releases them to the trading desk's blotter. Orders above a size threshold or keyed by hand need a second portfolio manager's check first.

next.condition: large or manual order needs a second check

steps.name: Second portfolio manager checks a large or manual order
steps.description: Another portfolio manager compares the order with the approved decision or trade file (security, side, quantity, account) and approves it in the system before it goes to the desk.

control.basis: Four-eyes check on large or manually keyed orders under the trade management policy (author's assumption)

evidence.note: Author's estimate of a common fat-finger control.

steps.name: Order goes to the trading desk
steps.description: The released order appears on the trading desk's blotter with the portfolio manager's instructions and becomes the desk's to execute.

evidence.note: Query rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Answer a trader's query on the order
steps.description: The trader reports a problem (limit away from the market, order large against volume, trading halt, news) and the portfolio manager decides to amend the order, confirm it as it is, or cancel it.

evidence.note: Portfolio managers work with traders on strategy; shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check fills against target positions
steps.description: The next morning the analyst compares the strategy's positions after execution with the target portfolio or index weights and flags names left unfilled or filled in the wrong account. Touch time is this order's share of work done for a whole rebalance list, so it is small per order.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; waiting covers the trading day.

steps.name: Decide on an unfilled residual or mismatch
steps.description: The portfolio manager decides whether an unfilled residual is still wanted (new order), can be left until the next rebalance, or whether a misallocated fill needs a correcting trade with operations.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Pre-trade compliance alert
exceptions.description: An order raises a warning or block; compliance overrides a false alert caused by reference data or sends the order back.

exceptions.name: Large fundamental stake to committee
exceptions.description: A large ownership stake goes to the Equities and Credit Investment Department Committee at its next meeting.

exceptions.name: Restricted name or inside information
exceptions.description: Compliance holds a fundamental trade because the company is on the restricted list or the team may hold inside information.

exceptions.name: Model rerun
exceptions.description: The portfolio manager or managing director rejects the factor trade list and the optimiser is rerun with changed constraints.

exceptions.name: Trader query
exceptions.description: The desk queries an order because of its limit, size or market conditions and the portfolio manager amends or cancels it.

exceptions.name: Corrective trade for a breach
exceptions.description: Compliance reports a guideline breach and the portfolio manager places a corrective trade.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the order need arising to the post-trade check
benchmarks.population: Orders of an institutional internal equity team mixing factor, index and fundamental strategies

evidence.note: No published measure. Factor and flow orders go out within a day or two; index orders wait for effective dates two to three weeks after announcement; fundamental orders wait for research and approvals.

benchmarks.unit: MSCI index reviews (two quarterly, two semi-annual in 2022)

benchmarks.population: The model manager Analyst, Fundamental Equities posting

evidence.note: Posting date outside the reference period.

pain_points.description: Bad or late reference data (new listings, share counts, classifications) causes model problems and false pre-trade compliance alerts that hold orders on busy days.

evidence.note: Organisation file notes false alerts from reference data.

pain_points.description: Trade lists move between the model, spreadsheets and the order system by file upload and re-keying, which invites fat-finger and account errors.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: Fundamental decisions wait for managing director and committee calendars while prices move.

evidence.note: Author estimate; committees were new in 2021.

pain_points.description: Index changes bunch at review effective dates, so a week's work lands on one close.

sources.title: The model manager 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: Read as the text copy saved under scratch/. Three equity pools and the public market alternatives pool ($29.2 billion pooled at end 2021); pooling brings operational efficiencies in day-to-day pool activities and cash management; public equities combine internal fundamental, factor (size, quality, value, momentum) and index strategies with external managers; fixed income ($17.2 billion) is managed internally for capital preservation and liquidity against FTSE Canada government indices; global credit ($6.0 billion) does not separate public and private credit, plans to internalise through direct co-investments, invested US$500 million with Antares (sponsor-backed middle-market direct lending) and US$500 million with Ares; PMA uses a managed account platform with 12 managers; Investment Policy Statements per strategy set permitted investments and restrictions; Management Investment Committee and three Investment Department Committees (Total Portfolio, Equities and Credit, Real Assets) approve up to thresholds; clean SOC 1 Type I report at 30 September 2021.

sources.title: The model manager 2022 Annual Report
sources.supports: Read as the text copy saved under scratch/. Investment Department Committees for Total Portfolio, Equities and Credit and Real Assets, co-chaired by Investments and Investment Risk with Legal and Responsible Investing, approve decisions up to thresholds; Management Investment Committee co-chaired by the CIO and CRO recommends anything needing Board approval.

sources.title: The model manager, Commission and Director decisions (exemption order)
sources.supports: Read as the text copy saved under scratch/. The model manager exempted from adviser registration on conditions; Board-approved policies must cover a compliance system, books and records, conflicts including front running, soft dollars and fairness in allocating investment opportunities among members and pools, prevention of investments that contravene restrictions set out in each investment management agreement, due diligence on sub-advisers, and due diligence on custodians and brokers before they hold or access assets.

sources.title: Asset Manager's Guide to SOC 1
sources.publisher: SIFMA Asset Management Group and Grant Thornton
sources.supports: Read as the text copy saved under scratch/. Baseline SOC 1 control objectives: trades properly authorised, settled and recorded in accordance with portfolio guidelines and account restrictions; contributions and distributions authorised by the client and processed accurately; other control areas include brokerage allocation (best execution, soft dollars, IPO and new issue allocation), broker selection and retention, trade aggregation, trade allocation, trade errors and guideline breaches.

sources.title: Public Equities (The model manager web page)
sources.supports: Passive strategy tracks a market benchmark for efficient liquidity; factor investing builds exposure to quality, value, momentum and low volatility; fundamental equities including large stakes, sometimes with board representation; external partnerships; a portfolio completion programme manages unintended concentrations; managing directors for factor investing and fundamental equity.

sources.title: Analyst - Fundamental Equities (The model manager job posting)
sources.supports: Analyst researches companies and industries, builds financial and valuation models (DCF, comparables, merger models), supports due diligence and investment reports, meets management teams and sell-side analysts, and works with Finance and Investment Operations on accounting for public equities; base pay CA$85,000 to $110,000 plus incentive.

sources.title: Trade Strategy and Execution (refresher reading)
sources.supports: Trade strategy depends on order, security, market and portfolio manager inputs including urgency and alpha decay; portfolio managers work with traders on strategy; liquidity-driven and index trades typically use closing prices; arrival price, VWAP and close benchmarks; implementation shortfall is the standard cost measure; regulators expect a written trade policy covering best execution, trade errors, eligible brokers and execution monitoring.

sources.title: Trading Controls: Prevention and Automation
sources.publisher: Deloitte UK (Ed Waller and Jaspreet Jhaj)
sources.supports: Preventative trading controls range from a pre-trade check or prompt to supervisory approval or a hard block; soft blocks can be too easily clicked through, raising fat-finger risk; regulatory or legal restrictions should never be breached while some internal limits allow judgement-based exceptions; manual detective controls are weaker.

sources.title: Index Review (MSCI web page)
sources.supports: MSCI index reviews take place in February, May, August and November; in 2022 February and August were quarterly index reviews and May and November semi-annual index reviews; each review has published announcement and effective dates.

assumptions: The unit is one single-security order. Work done once for a whole factor or index list (data checks, model runs, sign-off) is spread across the orders in the list, so per-order touch times on those steps are small.
Order shares by strategy (45% factor, 38% index and completion, 13% fundamental, 4% corrective) are the author's estimates; the model manager does not publish order counts.

The process map lists the annual plan, security reference data and compliance exceptions as triggers; scheduled model runs and index changes are counted under reference data and fundamental decisions under the plan's strategy mandate.
The senior managing director of equities and credit stands for the Equities and Credit Investment Department Committee; that role is in the organisation file but not in the process map's role list.
The compliance analyst is added for restricted list checks and alert reviews; it is not in the process map's role list.
Approval thresholds and the four-eyes rule on large orders are assumed; the model manager publishes only that approval authorities are defined.
Execution itself belongs to trade execution; the case waits through the trading day and ends with the next-morning post-trade check.
Loaded costs per hour come from the organisation file.
